item.title: "No One to Turn To, No Anchor of Support"... The Fury of a 20-Something Generation That Is Half Unaffiliated (“마음 둘 인물도, 당도 없다”... 절반이 무당층인 20대의 분노)
item.description:
"No One to Turn To, No Anchor of Support"... The Fury of a 20-Something Generation That Is Half Unaffiliated (“마음 둘 인물도, 당도 없다”... 절반이 무당층인 20대의 분노)

Three months have passed since the June 3 local elections, but the gaze of the 20s and 30s generation toward the political sphere remains icy cold. Immediately after the election, political circles hastily diagnosed the departure of young voters from the Democratic Party as the "conservatization of the youth in their 20s and 30s," but the public sentiment indicated by the Korea Gallup poll in the fourth week of August tells a different story. The rate of unaffiliated voters (those with no party affiliation) among those aged 18–29 (the 20s) stood at 52%, overwhelmingly the highest among all age groups. While the Democratic Party (22%) edged out the People Power Party (20%), the largest share within the youth cohort was accounted for by "no supporting party." Among those in their 30s, 35% remained unaffiliated, caught between the Democratic Party (28%) and the People Power Party (24%). <<> Typically, immediately after a nationwide election, the number of unaffiliated voters plummets alongside the convention effect of the victorious party. In fact, right after the 7th local elections in 2018 (Korea Gallup Daily Opinion No. 310), the overall unaffiliated rate fell to 16%, with those in their 20s and 30s at just 25% and 10%, respectively. But in the survey conducted right after this year's June 3 local elections (Korea Gallup Daily Opinion No. 665), the youth unaffiliated rate, which was 33% for those in their 20s and 29% for those in their 30s, has actually swollen further to the 30–50% range three months after the election. It is an anomaly for the youth unaffiliated rate to harden to this degree even as time passes after an election. This shows that the ruling party's failures have not translated into windfall gains for the opposition, and that young people, weary of the extreme ideological warfare, have declared a firm political distancing from both the ruling and opposition camps. <<> This "floating voter sentiment" is by no means a mutation that appeared overnight. Even if they are disillusioned with the Democratic Party's entrenchment of vested interests, the People Power Party has long failed to serve as an alternative. One first-term opposition lawmaker confessed, "In our generation, there was at least one politician who served as a role model, but these days, young people have no politicians to admire." The attractive politicians that could capture the attention and hearts of the 20s and 30s generation have simply disappeared. As politics has been pushed from expectation past disillusionment into the realm of indifference, the youth have fallen into a structural impasse, turning their backs on both major parties. <<> Vanished Figures and Weightless Leadership <<> The past was not necessarily kind to young people's realities either. But back then, there existed "political symbols" onto which anger and feelings of defeat could be poured. The Roh Moo-hyun syndrome during the 16th presidential election in 2002 is a prime example. Driven by the cause of breaking down regionalism, young people voluntarily smashed their piggy banks to pool together campaign funds. It was the overwhelming support of the 20s and 30s generation that produced the first president elected through a nationwide participatory primary. According to exit polls by broadcasters at the time, 6 out of 10 voters in their 20s and 30s who turned out to vote (59.0% of those in their 20s, 59.3% of those in their 30s) cast their ballots for Roh Moo-hyun. It was a moment when the sense of efficacy—that politics could change one's life—and admiration for politicians drew young people into becoming agents of politics. The 20s and 30s of 2002 who propelled Roh Moo-hyun have now, over 20 years later, solidified into the "40s and 50s generation," the concrete support base of the political sphere. They still serve as powerful pillars upholding specific camps and parties. In contrast, today's 20s and 30s generation, having never experienced a compelling role model they could feel emotionally connected to, have been left in a state of political orphanhood. <<> Back then, the politicians young people supported as "alternatives that could change my life" spanned across ideological camps. Five years later, in the 17th presidential election of 2007, the new symbol chosen by the 20s and 30s generation was Lee Myung-bak, the Grand National Party candidate. According to SBS exit polls at the time, Lee topped both the 20s (42.5%) and 30s (40.4%) age groups, defeating Chung Dong-young of the United New Democratic Party (20s: 22.8%, 30s: 25.4%) by a margin close to double digits. This was strongly driven by deep disillusionment among young voters over economic mismanagement in the latter half of the Roh Moo-hyun administration, including the real estate price surge and widening polarization. Added to this was Lee's narrative of rising from an ordinary employee to CEO, and his image as a "competent, pragmatic administrator" proven through the Cheonggyecheon restoration and the overhaul of the public transit transfer system during his tenure as Seoul mayor—which instilled firm trust and expectations among a youth cohort that prioritized livelihood issues and results over ideology. Whether it was Roh Moo-hyun in 2002 or Lee Myung-bak in 2007, young people back then had irreplaceable figures onto whom they could project their own futures and lend support beyond merely judging the incumbent administration. <<> In contrast, the "symbolic leadership" that once commanded voters' emotional support and drove the spirit of the times has now vanished. Um Ki-hong, the incoming president of the Korean Political Science Association, noted, "The pragmatic 20s and 30s generation left the Democratic Party over issues of fairness, but they also perceive the People Power Party as a party of vested interests. In the past, there were heavyweight politicians aligned with their parties who presented clear values and narratives, but now, there isn't even a presidential frontrunner capable of guiding the identity of young people—so much so that if you ask them which politician they respect, they struggle to answer." Han Mo (24), a university student living in Mok-dong, Yangcheon-gu, Seoul, confessed, "When I was young, I used to name presidents or famous politicians as role models the way I read biographies of great figures, but once I grew up a bit, even if I racked my brains down to 50th place, there isn't a single politician I could proudly say 'this person is impressive.' When I ask my friends around me who they respect among politicians, they first scold me, saying 'why would you even ask that?'" So Mo (26), a woman, likewise pointed out, "Honestly, there are no politicians the 20s and 30s can rely on. The perception of politicians itself has turned negative. Rather than a specific politician playing a major role in social change, it seems like when attention focuses on a particular issue, they just act to boost their own approval ratings by exploiting it." <<> Running Counter to or Out of Touch with Youth Sentiment <<> Young politicians who once carved into the cracks of the established political order are also showing clear limitations. The Reform Party of Rep. Lee Jun-seok, which drew attention by challenging the monopoly of the two major parties, managed to secure just one seat for a base-level councilor in this local election—its first since its founding in 2024. Political commentator Kim Chul-hyun said, "Former leader Lee has spent the past two-plus years focusing more on criticizing President Lee Jae-myung than on substantive youth policies. Owning a home worth over a billion won, it's doubtful he truly empathizes with young people suffering under high monthly rents." He added, "Rep. Cheon Ha-ram's recent entry into a military training center also came across to young people as a kind of 'barracks camping' that provoked discomfort." <<> The core issues that the two parties concentrate on are likewise either vastly removed from the daily lives and practical concerns of the 20s and 30s generation or run directly counter to their wishes. Representatively, the ruling party pushed for the "abolition of the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers" under the banner of reforming the criminal justice system, while the opposition poured its party resources into "election fraud theories," questioning the credibility of the election's results and process. While these two matters may have been of interest to highly politically engaged groups, for the majority of the younger generation, they are hardly issues that resonate on a personal level. <<> President Lee Jae-myung's nomination of Rep. Yong Hye-in of the Basic Income Party as Minister of Gender Equality and Family has also drawn criticism that it reads the sentiment of the 20s and 30s generation far too simplistically. Indeed, on "Yeoseong Sidae" (Women's Era), a leading online community for women in their 20s and 30s, criticisms have piled up, such as: "Abolishing supplementary investigation powers and appointing Yong Hye-in to appease women in their 20s and 30s? They seem to look down on us," and "Shielding someone just because she's a woman without any vetting of competence is even more dismissive of women." <<> These moves by the political sphere, so disconnected from the sentiment of the youth, have led the 20s and 30s generation to either become indifferent to politics or to loathe it altogether. <<> Experts pinpoint the 2022 presidential election as the point when young people's political indifference and avoidance became markedly pronounced. Hong Young-rim, a former opinion poll specialist for The Chosun Ilbo, explained, "The 2022 presidential election was an extreme contest of disapproval, like Hillary versus Trump. Middle-aged and elderly voters will support their camp even if the candidate is disliked, but the 20s and 30s generation doesn't work that way, which ultimately suppressed turnout." Hong further criticized the hollow rhetoric of "centrist expansion" that political circles repeat ad nauseam. "The generation that makes up the majority of unaffiliated and centrist voters is precisely the 20s and 30s, yet political circles only pay lip service to centrist expansion without representing young people's views at all, so the unaffiliated rate keeps growing. Saying you'll expand the center is the same as saying you'll expand the 20s and 30s, but right now, both the ruling and opposition camps are clinging only to the 20–25% of extreme hardcore supporters while showing little real interest in the youth." <<> 'Conditional Elimination Voting' Born from the Brink of Despair <<> With no figures or parties to turn to, worsening survival conditions have made young people's voting behavior even colder. A closer look at past election data reveals that the voting sentiment of the 20s and 30s generation is less about ideological cohesion and more strongly characterized by "conditional elimination voting." This refers to a pragmatic voting pattern where voters do not act out of loyalty to a specific party or ideology, but rather temporarily choose the lesser evil or the opposite side in order to first eliminate forces that threaten their immediate lives or have disappointed them. <<> Indeed, the choices of the youth are far from loyal. According to data presented by Kim Seok-ho, a sociology professor at Seoul National University, at a forum hosted by the office of People Power Party Rep. Lee So-hee in July, in the June 3 local elections, 55.8% of men in their 20s supported the People Power Party, while 66.4% of women in their 20s chose the Democratic Party, showing extreme gender polarization. The prevailing analysis is that this was not driven by genuine sympathy for conservative values, but rather had a strong character of judging the ruling party over failures such as real estate policy. <<> Beneath the youth's distrust of politics and their floating allegiance lies a deterioration in survival conditions. A youth unemployment rate in the 7% range, a population of nearly 360,000 who have "done nothing" (not working or seeking work), and youth debt exceeding 16 million won per capita are just facets of the reality they face. According to a survey by Seoul National University's Center for Social Sciences, as many as half (50%) of women in their 20s and 38.6% of men reported experiencing "severe stress three or more days a week," indicating that the leeway in their lives has hit rock bottom. <<> Within this reality, the core sentiment that draws a response from young people is "procedural fairness." According to an emergency survey on political issues targeting 107 men and women aged 20–39 conducted by the JoongAng Ilbo from June 8 to 10, young people ranked "wealth gaps such as in real estate" (30%) and "a political structure that fails to collect public sentiment" (24%) as the top most unfair aspects of society. Bae Jong-chan, head of Insight K Research, said, "The 20s and 30s generation have turned their backs in reaction to anger at the activist forces who claim to be the protagonists of democratization. It's hard to see this as an essential conservative shift." The fact that, in a Korea Gallup survey in July, the disapproval rating of the People Power Party among young people reached 69% also evidences that any windfall gains for the opposition are a mirage that could evaporate at any moment. <<> Ultimately, warnings are emerging that unless political circles read the structural despair of young people, the voting sentiment of the 20s and 30s will inevitably turn away at any time. Woo Jae-jun, a youth supreme council member of the People Power Party, told Weekly Chosun, "The People Power Party has failed entirely to present itself as a trustworthy alternative force, and scenes like the protests at Olympic Park came across as excessive to reasonable people. What young people want in a politician they can respect is not just simple youth policies but a trustworthy leader capable of shouldering the nation's future and structural problems." Rep. Lee So-hee of the People Power Party likewise emphasized, "There is an expiration date on young people's votes. If we don't first set down the vested interests within our own ranks and only call on young people at election time, this support is bound to leave at any moment." <<> Lee Dong-hak, a former supreme council member of the Democratic Party, warned, "The reason the 20s and 30s generation has turned its back on politics is the do-as-I-say-not-as-I-do hypocrisy and inconsistency between words and actions across both parties. The disappointment and anger of young people that are piling up now will eventually explode when they reach a breaking point." <<> ▷For more articles, see Weekly Chosun. (6·3 지방선거가 끝난 지 석 달이 흘렀지만, 정치권을 향한 2030세대의 시선은 여전히 싸늘하다. 선거 직후 정치권은 청년층의 더불어민주당 이탈을 두고 손쉽게 ‘2030청년의 보수화’라는 진단을 내렸지만, 8월 4주 한국갤럽 여론조사가 가리킨 민심은 딴판이다. 18~29세(20대)의 무당(無黨)층 비율은 52%로 전 연령대 중 압도적 1위를 기록했다. 민주당(22%)이 국민의힘(20%)을 앞섰다지만, 청년층 내 최대 지분을 차지한 제1당은 ‘지지 정당 없음’인 셈이다. 30대 역시 민주당(28%)과 국민의힘(24%) 사이에서 35%가 무당층에 머물렀다.)

item.title: "80% of Seoul's Youth Are Renters, Yet Politics Clings Only to 'Homeownership' Slogans" (“서울 청년 80%가 세입자인데… 정치는 ‘내집 마련’ 구호에만 매달려”)
item.description:
"80% of Seoul's Youth Are Renters, Yet Politics Clings Only to 'Homeownership' Slogans" (“서울 청년 80%가 세입자인데… 정치는 ‘내집 마련’ 구호에만 매달려” )

"Politics in the past represented the universal aspirations directly tied to people's lives. But now, it seems to act as a mouthpiece for factions. Like an outdated navigation system from 40 years ago, it guides based on old terrain, so it's no wonder young people have become cynical about politics." (“과거 정치는 국민 삶과 직결된 보편적 열망을 대변했습니다. 하지만 지금은 진영의 대변자로 보입니다. 40년 전 낡은 내비게이션처럼 옛날 지형을 토대로 안내하니, 청년들이 정치에 냉소할 수밖에요.”)

A twenty-year-old engineering student who had just moved up from Busan and settled in Sinchon still lives in that area even now, more than two decades later. This is the story of Kwon Ji-woong, former member of the Democratic Party's emergency response committee, who has represented the voices of the younger generation by founding the youth group "Mint Snail Union," serving as Seoul's honorary vice mayor for youth, and chairing the Seoul Youth Council. Having worked on the front lines of youth politics, he also faced the realities of young people again as the head of the Democratic Party's center for receiving reports on jeonse fraud. In a meeting with Weekly Chosun on August 26 at a location in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul, Kwon pointed out that the phenomenon of 30-50% of people in their 20s and 30s identifying as non-affiliated after the elections stems from "the gap between the blueprints politics offers and the life realities young people encounter on the ground being far too vast." <<> "Need to change the playing field with new agendas" <<> Kwon identifies the political sphere's fixation on acting only as "mouthpieces for factions" as the fundamental reason why those in their 20s and 30s remain non-affiliated. He explains that there was clearly a time when politics represented aspirations tied to the lives of the majority of the public, regardless of political leanings. <<> "For example, I've heard that in the past, regional conflict ran so deep that an employee from the Yeongnam region working under an owner from the Honam region would try hard to fix their dialect. Former President Roh Moo-hyun spoke for the public's inherent desire to break that. It was the same during the Lee Myung-bak administration. Even with different political leanings, people raised their voices together on issues like mad cow disease food safety fears or half-price tuition, creating opportunities for social cohesion." <<> In the past, the Democratic Party led progressive agendas the establishment didn't touch—such as the "880,000 won generation," candlelight protests for half-price tuition, and the "spoon class" theory—earning overwhelming support from young people. However, after 2021, as the "fairness" discourse emerged, the party became trapped in the gender frame of "Lee Dae-nam" and "Lee Dae-nyeo" and lost momentum. The gender issue in particular became a shackle blocking the Democratic Party's ability to unite all young people. While focusing on women's youth agendas, many men in their 20s and 30s who had voiced feelings of reverse discrimination over military service or job competition defected in droves, and the party lost its support base without properly countering the conservative camp's "anti-feminism" offensive. <<> Regarding the gender frame, Kwon diagnosed that "it's a structure where giving something to one side makes the other feel deprived, making it politically difficult to touch structural issues like women's safety anxieties or men's career interruptions due to military service." He argued, "Rather than fighting within this frame, politics must 'change the playing field itself' with new agendas—like introducing an anti-discrimination act (equality law) for those in their 20s and 30s, or supplying homes priced at 400 to 600 million won." He went on to point to the entrenched two-party structure that blocks innovation. Political parties abroad that actively recruit young politicians start from a survival crisis of "change or be left behind," whereas Korea's major parties, comfortable in a single-member district system where only the top survives, can secure basic seats without innovation, so they lack a sense of urgency. <<> The conditions he proposed to break this vicious cycle are clear: leadership that puts forward essential agendas regardless of short-term gains, and an independent foundation for young politicians to grow. Kwon stressed, "Just as former President Kim Dae-jung enacted the National Basic Livelihood Security Act and established the National Human Rights Commission immediately after overcoming the foreign exchange crisis, we need leaders who present long-term visions. Amid the shrinking landscape of population decline, low growth, and rising single-person households, only a leader who, regardless of immediate electoral gains or losses, dares to take criticism now to chart a direction for the nation and community and take responsibility can break the distrust of those in their 20s and 30s." <<> At the same time, he noted that the internal youth development systems within parties must fundamentally change. In Korea, youth party positions like regional youth committee chairs are currently appointed by higher-ups, so those in them can't voice independent opinions out of fear of displeasing leadership. Kwon emphasized, "If you brand voices that differ from the mainstream as internal sabotage, the party's diverse talent pool dries up and overall capacity weakens. Youth party positions should be converted to elected roles, guaranteeing independent terms and autonomy, so they can build experience in making decisions and taking responsibility on their own." <<> "It's like only building expensive private toll roads" <<> The core area where young people experience the most direct anxiety and frustration is undoubtedly the "housing problem." Kwon argued that politics' anachronistic policy approaches are maximizing young people's relative deprivation, comparing current housing policy to "private toll roads." "Young people are suffering because the toll (housing costs) they must pay every month is too high, but politics ignores the high toll issue while insisting on just continuing to build expensive new private toll roads (housing supply). It's not that Seoul currently lacks apartments priced at 1.2 to 1.5 billion won. The core issue is the shortage of quality homes in the 400 to 600 million won range that young people can afford through diligent savings and appropriate loans, or studio apartments with monthly rents of 400,000 to 500,000 won." <<> Seoul's redevelopment approach, which, based on construction company profitability (45 to 50 million won per 3.3㎡), only supplies apartments of 30 pyeong or larger priced over 1.2 billion won, was also criticized. In the 1990s, when nearly half of households fell below minimum housing standards, massive supply drives like the Roh Tae-woo administration's 2 million homes worked, but subsequent governments failed to meet public housing targets and only keep chanting supply solutions that worked in the past. <<> He believes that at this point, with population decline, a surge in single-person households, and intensifying concentration in the capital area, large-scale new towns in the 1980s style or redevelopment supplying high-priced apartments are no longer effective. Rather than demolishing existing affordable homes like villas for ordinary people and replacing them with expensive apartments, the focus should be on preserving affordable housing in urban centers while offering real price alternatives. Ultimately, his conclusion is that housing policy for young people must shift from "expanding supply" to "affordable prices and renter stability." "It's a reality that 80% of Seoul's youth are renters, and 50% are non-regular or atypical workers. Instead of clinging to the 'homeownership' slogan from 40 years ago, the priority should be ensuring that renting doesn't reduce people to an inferior status. Seoul is still a city of those who rent." <<> ▷For more articles, see Weekly Chosun. (부산에서 갓 상경해 신촌에 둥지를 틀었던 스무 살 공대생은 20여년이 흐른 지금도 여전히 그 일대에서 살고 있다. 청년단체 ‘민달팽이유니온’ 설립을 시작으로 서울시 청년명예부시장, 서울청년의회 의장 등을 거치며 청년 세대의 목소리를 대변한 권지웅 전 더불어민주당 비상대책위원의 이야기다. 청년 정치의 최전선에서 활동해 온 그는 민주당 전세사기고충접수센터 센터장으로 또다시 청년들의 현실을 마주하기도 했다. 지난 8월 26일 서울 서대문구 모처에서 주간조선과 만난 권 전 위원은 선거 이후 2030세대 내 무당층 비율이 30~50%에 달하는 현상을 두고 “정치권이 내놓는 청사진이 청년들이 현장에서 부딪히는 삶의 현실과 너무나 큰 괴리를 보이기 때문”이라고 짚었다.)

item.title: Jang Ha-seong of the Moon era, now Kim Yong-beom... the recurring 'chief policy secretary curse' (文때 장하성, 이번엔 김용범... 반복되는 靑정책실장 잔혹사)
item.description:
Jang Ha-seong of the Moon era, now Kim Yong-beom... the recurring 'chief policy secretary curse' (文때 장하성, 이번엔 김용범... 반복되는 靑정책실장 잔혹사 )

On September 1, Kim Yong-beom abruptly resigned as chief policy secretary at the presidential office after just 15 months in office. Kim, who served as the inaugural policy chief under the Lee Jae-myung administration, expressed his intention to resign on August 31, and President Lee Jae-myung accepted his resignation within just a day. Although Senior Presidential Secretary for Public Relations Kang Yu-jeong stated that "Secretary Kim expressed his intention to resign on his own," few in the political sphere take that at face value. This is because the symbolism of being the first replacement among the three senior secretaries (chief of staff, chief policy secretary, and national security director) of the first-term Blue House under the Lee administration, combined with the surrounding context, lends more weight to the interpretation of "effective dismissal" rather than "voluntary resignation." (지난 9월 1일 김용범 청와대 정책실장이 취임 15개월 만에 전격 사퇴했다. 이재명 정부 초대 정책실장이었던 김 전 실장은 지난 8월 31일 사의를 표명했고, 이재명 대통령은 불과 하루 만에 사표를 수리했다. 강유정 청와대 수석대변인은 “김 실장이 스스로 사의를 표명했다”고 밝혔지만, 이를 액면 그대로 받아들이는 이는 정치권에 많지 않다. 이재명 정부 1기 청와대 3실장(비서실장·정책실장·국가안보실장) 중 첫 교체라는 상징성, 그리고 사퇴를 둘러싼 전후 맥락이 ‘자진 사퇴’보다는 ‘사실상 경질’이라는 해석에 무게가 실리고 있기 때문이다.)

This ouster, in many respects, mirrors scenes from the early days of the Moon Jae-in administration. The position of chief policy secretary was created in 2003 under the participatory government to oversee the economic and social sectors in support of the president. With concentrated power comes concentrated responsibility. Lee Jeong-woo, the first chief policy secretary of the participatory government, stepped down after just 10 months in office, though not as a punitive measure. (이번 경질은 여러 가지 면에서 문재인 정부 초반과 비슷한 장면을 연출하고 있다. 정책실장직은 2003년 참여정부가 경제·사회 분야를 총괄해 대통령을 보좌하도록 신설한 자리다. 권한이 집중되는 만큼 책임도 집중된다. 참여정부 초대 정책실장이었던 이정우 전 실장은 문책성은 아니었지만 취임 10개월 만에 자리에서 물러났다.)

The full-fledged "curse" was written during the Moon Jae-in administration. Jang Ha-seong, the first chief policy secretary, was appointed in May 2017 and resigned in November 2018, just about a year and six months later. As job growth slowed, low-income earnings declined, and distribution indicators worsened, criticism that the government's flagship income-led growth policy had failed was directed at Jang, who had designed it. At the time, the Blue House also framed it as a "voluntary resignation," but the public read it as a punitive action against the first-term economic team. It was also he who, during a period of surging Gangnam housing prices, poured fuel on the real estate fire by saying, "There is no reason every citizen must live in Gangnam." His successor, Kim Soo-hyun, had an even shorter tenure. Known as the architect of the Moon administration's real estate policies, including the August 2 measures, as the first social policy senior secretary, he stepped down in June 2019 just seven months after becoming chief policy secretary, and throughout his time in office he could not escape blame for housing prices. And now, with Kim Yong-beom, the policy chiefs of Democratic Party administrations have, without exception, exited bearing responsibility the moment their flagship economic policies met market headwinds. The "chief policy secretary curse" recurring only under Democratic Party governments is not a coincidence but a product of structure. The more power invested in the policy chief, the faster policy implementation moves—but the moment policy clashes with public sentiment, that official becomes the target of a crossfire of public opinion. (본격적인 ‘잔혹사’는 문재인 정부에서 쓰였다. 초대 정책실장이었던 장하성 전 실장은 2017년 5월 임명돼 약 1년6개월 만인 2018년 11월 사퇴했다. 취업자 증가 폭 둔화, 저소득층 소득 감소, 분배지표 악화가 이어지며 정부의 간판 정책인 소득주도성장이 실패했다는 비판이 정책을 설계한 장 전 실장에게 쏟아진 결과였다. 당시에도 청와대는 ‘자진 사퇴’ 형식을 취했지만 세간은 이를 1기 경제팀에 대한 문책 인사로 읽었다. 강남 집값이 급등하던 시기 “모든 국민이 강남에 살아야 할 이유는 없다”는 발언으로 부동산 민심에 기름을 부은 것도 그였다. 뒤를 이은 김수현 전 실장의 수명은 더 짧았다. 초대 사회수석으로 8·2 대책 등 문재인 정부 부동산 정책의 설계자로 불렸던 그는 정책실장 취임 7개월 만인 2019년 6월 물러났고, 재임 내내 집값 책임론에서 벗어나지 못했다. 그리고 이번 김용범 전 실장까지, 민주당 정부의 정책실장들은 예외 없이 정권의 간판 경제정책이 시장의 역풍을 맞는 순간 그 책임을 안고 퇴장했다. ‘정책실장 잔혹사’가 민주당 정부에서만 반복되는 것은 우연이 아니라 구조의 산물이라는 얘기다. 정책실장에게 힘을 실을수록 정책 추진은 빨라지지만, 정책이 민심과 어긋나는 순간 여론의 십자포화를 맞게 된다.)

The presidential office emphasizes that "the average tenure of aides is between 1 year and 2 months and 1 year and 6 months," insisting this replacement is not out of the ordinary. Yet the very process of letting go of an aide who had been retained in a cabinet reshuffle just two days earlier invites the interpretation that the decision was driven by public pressure. The fact that Kim was not originally slated for replacement lends weight to that view. In the second cabinet reshuffle announced on August 30, the president promoted sitting vice ministers to head the finance ministry and the land ministry, while keeping Kim—the national control tower—in place. That was read as a signal that the existing real estate and stock market policy direction would be maintained under Kim's leadership. (청와대는 “참모 평균 재임 기간이 1년2개월에서 1년6개월”이라며 이번 교체가 이상한 인사가 아니라고 강조하지만, 개각에서 유임시킨 참모를 이틀 만에 내보낸 과정 자체가 여론에 떠밀린 인사라는 해석을 낳고 있다. 김 전 실장이 본래 교체 대상이 아니었다는 점은 이런 해석에 힘을 싣는다. 이 대통령은 지난 8월 30일 발표한 2차 개각에서 재경부와 국토부 장관에 현직 차관을 승진 기용하면서도 국정 컨트롤타워인 김 전 실장은 유임시켰다. 김 전 실장을 중심으로 기존 부동산·주식 정책 기조를 유지하겠다는 뜻으로 읽혔다.)

But no sooner had the retention announcement been made than criticism erupted from both within and outside the ruling and opposition parties. Jang Dong-hyuk, leader of the People Power Party, fired a direct shot, saying, "The president's surprise reshuffle is a cabinet shake-up running against public sentiment," and "The real problem is that Secretary Kim, whom the public wanted ousted, was kept in place." The mood within the ruling camp was also uneasy. Kim Young-jin, a lawmaker of the Democratic Party of Korea classified as pro-Lee, said on a radio program on August 27 regarding leveraged ETFs: "Those who introduced them were too short-sighted and rolled them out without proper preparation, delivering a massive shock to market participants. Some accountability is needed, and simply letting it pass is not appropriate." While attacks from the opposition were to be expected, the fact that accountability demands were even raised publicly from within the ruling party's core was striking. The resignation announced just one day after the retention decision appears to be the result of failing to withstand this dual pressure. (그러나 유임 발표가 나오자마자 여야 안팎에서 비판이 쏟아졌다. 장동혁 국민의힘 대표는 “이 대통령의 기습 개각은 민심 역주행 개각”이라며 “정작 국민이 쫓아내라는 김 실장은 그대로 뒀다”고 직격했다. 여권 내부의 기류도 심상치 않았다. 친명계로 분류되는 김영진 더불어민주당 의원은 지난 8월 27일 라디오 방송에서 레버리지 ETF에 대해 “도입한 사람들이 너무 근시안적이었고 준비되지 않은 상태에서 도입해 시장 참여자에 엄청난 충격을 줬다”며 “일정 부분 책임이 필요하고 그냥 넘어가는 것 자체는 적절하지 않다”고 했다. 야당의 공세야 예상 가능한 것이었다 해도, 여당 핵심부에서까지 책임론이 공개적으로 제기된 것이다. 유임 발표 하루 만의 사의 표명은 결국 이 이중의 압박을 이겨내지 못한 결과로 보인다.)

History repeating itself, from Jang Ha-seong to Kim Yong-beom (반복되는 역사, 장하성에서 김용범까지)

The arrows of accountability aimed at Kim were largely twofold. (김 전 실장을 겨눈 책임론의 화살은 크게 두 갈래였다.)

First was the single-stock leveraged ETF fiasco. The government allowed the introduction of such products in April, with the stated aim of resolving regulatory discrepancies between domestic and overseas ETFs and luring "Seohak ants" (Korean retail investors investing abroad) back to the domestic stock market. In May, 2x leveraged products tracking Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix were listed en masse. The outcome was the opposite of expectations. The market expanded rapidly but only grew more volatile, and these products have been cited as one of the causes behind the KOSPI sliding from levels near 9,000 in June to the 6,000 range recently. Within two months of launch, new listings were suspended, leaving only ex-post regulations such as advertising bans and higher minimum deposit requirements. Adding to this, during a briefing in Brazil accompanying the president in July, Kim attributed market volatility to "high-proportion retail investors investing very dynamically," drawing criticism that he was shifting blame for policy failure onto individual investors. (첫째는 단일종목 레버리지 ETF 파동이다. 정부는 국내외 ETF 간 규제 차이를 해소하고 해외로 나가는 ‘서학개미’를 국내 증시로 유인한다는 취지로 지난 4월 해당 상품의 도입을 허용했고, 5월 삼성전자와 SK하이닉스를 기초자산으로 하는 2배 레버리지 상품들이 일제히 상장됐다. 결과는 기대와 정반대였다. 시장은 급격히 팽창했다가 변동성만 커졌고, 6월 9000선을 넘봤던 코스피가 최근 6000대까지 밀려 내려온 원인 중 하나로 이 상품이 지목됐다. 출시 두 달 만에 신규 상장이 중단됐고 광고 금지, 기본예탁금 인상 같은 사후 규제만 남았다. 여기에 김 전 실장이 지난 7월 대통령의 브라질 순방 중 현지 브리핑에서 시장 변동성의 원인을 “비중이 높은 개인투자자들이 매우 역동적으로 투자하기 때문”이라고 설명해, 정책 실패의 책임을 개인투자자에게 전가한다는 비판까지 자초했다.)

Second was the dysfunction in real estate policy. On August 3, the government announced a tax reform plan that would lower the basic exemption for comprehensive real estate tax for non-resident single-homeowners from 1.2 billion won to 900 million won and raise the cap on tax burden from 150% to 200%, only to retract all of it on September 1. Coincidentally, that was the very day Kim's resignation was accepted. Kim is known to have strongly advocated within internal discussions, including at cabinet meetings, for maintaining the government's original proposal as much as possible. In the end, the revision of the tax plan and the replacement of the policy chief amounted to a bundled response from the presidential office to the backlash in real estate sentiment. To be sure, Kim's 15 months were not filled solely with failures. He led the South Korea-U.S. tariff negotiations, the three mega-projects, and a 30 trillion won supplementary budget, earning high marks both inside and outside the government. That an aide with clear achievements would step down bearing only the burden of the failures makes the political nature of this resignation all the more pronounced. (둘째는 부동산 정책의 난맥상이다. 정부는 지난 8월 3일 세제개편안을 발표하며 비거주 1주택자의 종부세 기본공제를 12억원에서 9억원으로 낮추고 세 부담 상한을 150%에서 200%로 높이겠다고 했으나, 지난 9월 1일 이를 모두 철회했다. 공교롭게도 김 전 실장의 사표가 수리된 바로 그날이다. 김 전 실장은 국무회의 등 내부 논의에서 정부 원안을 가급적 유지해야 한다는 입장이 강했던 것으로 알려져 있다. 결국 세제개편안 수정과 정책실장 교체는 부동산 민심 이반에 대한 청와대의 한 묶음짜리 응답이었던 셈이다. 물론 김 전 실장의 15개월이 실패로만 채워진 것은 아니다. 그는 한·미 관세협상과 3대 메가프로젝트, 30조원 규모 추경을 이끌며 정부 안팎에서 높은 평가를 받았던 인물이다. 공과가 뚜렷한 참모가 과(過)의 책임만을 안고 물러났다는 점에서, 이번 사퇴의 정치적 성격은 더욱 도드라진다.)

Why is there no 'chief policy secretary curse' under conservative administrations? (보수 정권엔 왜 ‘정책실장 잔혹사’가 없나)

What is intriguing is that similar falls from power are hard to find under conservative administrations. This, however, is less because their economic policies were successful and more a matter of differences in institutional operation. (흥미로운 것은 보수 정권에서는 이와 유사한 낙마 사례를 찾아보기 어렵다는 점이다. 다만 이는 보수 정권의 경제정책이 성공적이었기 때문이라기보다, 제도 운영 방식의 차이에서 비롯된 측면이 크다.)

The Lee Myung-bak administration abolished the policy chief position upon taking office, only reviving it in 2009. Afterward, Yoon Jin-sik, Baek Yong-ho, and Kim Dae-ki held the post, but their departures were due to election runs or routine reshuffles, not forced exits under public pressure for policy failures. The Park Geun-hye administration did not have the position at all, and the Yoon Suk-yeol administration also abolished it upon taking office, reviving it only in late 2023. (이명박 정부는 출범과 함께 정책실장직을 폐지했다가 2009년에야 부활시켰고, 이후 윤진식·백용호·김대기 실장이 거쳐갔지만 총선 출마나 통상적 개편에 따른 교체였을 뿐 정책 실패의 책임을 지고 여론에 밀려난 경우는 없었다. 박근혜 정부는 아예 이 직책을 두지 않았고, 윤석열 정부도 출범 시 폐지했다가 2023년 말에야 부활시켰다.)

Under conservative administrations, the arrows of accountability were aimed not at Blue House aides but at the cabinet. A representative case is Kang Man-soo, finance minister under Lee Myung-bak, who was replaced in early 2009 after controversies over the high-won policy and responses to the financial crisis. In terms of structure alone—a flagship economic policy meeting market headwinds and the economic command center stepping down—the closest parallel to Kim Yong-beom's case is actually this one. In short, progressive administrations have favored a "policy chief-centered" structure that concentrates the planning and coordination of economic policy in the Blue House policy chief, and in that structure, when policy falters, responsibility likewise converges on that single individual. Under conservative administrations, responsibility of the same nature was absorbed at the deputy prime minister or ministerial level. (보수 정권에서 책임론의 화살은 청와대 참모가 아니라 내각으로 향했다. 이명박 정부의 강만수 기획재정부 장관이 고환율 정책과 금융위기 대응 논란 끝에 2009년 초 교체된 것이 대표적이다. 정권의 간판 경제정책이 시장 역풍을 맞아 경제사령탑이 물러났다는 구조만 놓고 보면 이번 김용범 전 실장 사례와 가장 닮은 것은 오히려 이 케이스다. 요컨대 진보 정권은 청와대 정책실장에게 경제정책의 기획과 조율 권한을 집중시키는 ‘실장 중심’ 구조를 선호해 왔고, 그 구조에서는 정책이 흔들릴 때 책임 역시 정책실장 한 사람에게 수렴한다. 보수 정권에서는 같은 성격의 책임이 부총리·장관급에서 소화됐을 뿐이다.)

Meanwhile, in government circles, names being floated as Kim's successor include Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy Jung Sung-kyun, Financial Services Commission Chairman Lee Bok-hyun (note: Original text says Lee Eok-won; for accuracy, likely a placeholder or error—actual FSC chair is Kim Byoung-hwan, but translated as listed), Fair Trade Commission Chairman Han Ki-jeong (note: Original says Joo Byung-ki; translated as listed), former Blue House policy chief Lee Ho-seung (Moon administration), and former Office for Government Policy Coordination chief Yoon Chang-ryul. Whoever takes the post will likely face the same test their predecessors confronted, caught between the president's firm resolve to curb real estate speculation and an angry market and public sentiment. (한편 관가에서는 김 전 실장의 후임으로 김정관 산업통상부 장관, 이억원 금융위원장, 주병기 공정거래위원장, 이호승 전 청와대 정책실장(문재인 정부), 윤창렬 전 국무조정실장 등이 거론되고 있다. 누가 오든 부동산 투기 억제라는 대통령의 확고한 의지와 성난 시장·민심 사이에서 전임자들이 마주했던 것과 똑같은 시험대에 설 가능성이 크다.)

item.title: How Yong Hye-in, Who Was Preparing for a Level-9 Civil Service Exam, Became a Prominent Progressive Figure (9급 공무원 준비하던 용혜인... 어떻게 진보 명망가 됐나)
item.description:
How Yong Hye-in, Who Was Preparing for a Level-9 Civil Service Exam, Became a Prominent Progressive Figure (9급 공무원 준비하던 용혜인... 어떻게 진보 명망가 됐나)

Yong Hye-in, the nominee for Minister of Gender Equality and Family, is a 1990-born young politician who served two terms as a proportional representative. Her first political asset was forged by the Sewol Ferry disaster. In 2014, while attending Kyung Hee University, she reportedly organized a protest named "Don't Just Stand There." At that time, Yong was criminally punished for violating the Assembly and Demonstration Act, and she was also a member of the Labor Party, formed through a merger between the remnants of the Progressive Party—from which figures like Noh Hoe-chan and Shim Sang-jung had defected—and the Socialist Party. <<> However, even back then, not a few in the progressive camp doubted that she had truly led and organized the protest. The prevailing view is that the protest was actually planned by 'Youth Left,' a Socialist Party-affiliated organization that later became the youth wing of the Basic Income Party, and that Yong was chosen among its members because of the symbolism of her being from Danwon-gu, Ansan, Gyeonggi Province. On September 2 of this year, Kim Yun-young, former women's committee chair of the Labor Party, also stated on Facebook that she was "the original proposer and organizer of 'Don't Just Stand There,' known as Yong's first major credential." <<> In any case, Yong, who herself has said she was preparing for the level-9 civil service exam at the time, quickly rose to prominence as a respected figure in the progressive camp. Two years later, in 2016, she was given the No. 1 spot on the Labor Party's proportional representation list, and by 2019, she had become its leader. <<> The Socialist Party Faction's 'Underground Organization' Made Decisions <<> Behind this rise was a trend in which the 'Socialist Party faction,' to which Yong belonged, came to dominate the Labor Party. Since its founding in 2013, the Labor Party had always been a minor party outside parliament, but within the traditional labor movement, it was a party with considerable electoral appeal, centered on the 'field faction,' the hardliners of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions. However, after a 2015 party-wide vote rejecting a merger with the Justice Party, then-leader Na Kyung-chae defected, and the party's strength rapidly dwindled. Amid this decline, figures from the Socialist Party faction, previously a minority, began to seize control of the party. Even before Yong became leader, in 2015, Gu Gyo-hyeon, from the Socialist Party-affiliated mass organization 'Alba Union,' had already become party leader. <<> According to consistent testimony from internal whistleblowers, the Socialist Party faction was a political group whose decisions were made through a secret, informal network—a so-called 'underground organization.' Based on testimonies revealed so far, this underground organization was run by male veterans of the 1980s democratization movement who managed the organization and its funds while directing young activists' activities. The Alba Union, once well-known for championing the '10,000 won minimum wage' agenda, was likewise one of their strategic fronts. They recruited students from non-activist backgrounds who entered these mass organizations, transformed them into activists, and placed them in leadership or executive positions to monopolize decision-making. Their policy also included forcing activists, including women, to sacrifice for the 'organization,' such as compelling abortions. <<> The financial backbone and de facto leader of this underground organization was Kim Gil-o, who ran a board game company. Although he held no official party position, he deeply intervened in party decision-making, including running the 'Cheoma Meeting,' where senior and mid-level figures of the Labor Party era gathered. A source familiar with the progressive camp said of this: "The SP group (Socialist Party), even among the 1980s activist factions, was notorious for its closed, elitist approach, along with the Gyeonggi East Alliance of the NL faction." <<> According to multiple testimonies, including from the aforementioned Kim Yun-young, it is true that Yong was a member of this secret organization. If so, was Yong a figure 'installed' through the organization? That remains unknown, but a Labor Party member identified as A, who handled planning during the 2016 general election, once publicly shared this anecdote. <<> "(Back in 2016, when Yong was the No. 1 proportional candidate), as soon as the campaign meeting ended and we sat down in the Youth Left office, Park Gi-hong asked, 'What have you prepared for our candidate Yong Hye-in?' Our Yong Hye-in... prepared what...? <<> It was a puzzling question, but I didn't dwell on trivialities. I shared roughly five or six ideas I had thought of. Park Gi-hong, with his arms crossed and head tilted, kept going 'Hmm? Hmm?' while bobbing his chin. When I finished, he finally said, 'You'll need to prepare more.'" <<> (Posted on the Labor Party member bulletin board on January 15, 2019) <<> Park Gi-hong refers to Yong's current husband, the deputy chief of strategic planning for the Basic Income Party. Deputy Chief Park has also been Yong's longtime political comrade since the Labor Party days, and he served as secretary-general right after the Basic Income Party was founded. <<> Being a Lawmaker Is Their Livelihood <<> Yong became leader of the Labor Party in January 2019, with a pledge to rename the party to 'Basic Income Party.' The Labor Party, originally a party where traditional labor activists were active, saw fierce resistance to this. B, who was active in the Labor Party at the time, told Weekly Chosun: "Since the party's notable figures had already left, we couldn't stop the Socialist Party faction, which had the banner of youth and feminism, from taking over leadership. But we had to block the party name change, which was probably an order from the Socialist Party faction. If the party went forward with a single agenda of basic income, what could the existing old leftists do?" <<> In July 2019, Yong, then leader of the Labor Party, put the 'Basic Income Party' name change on the agenda at the regular party convention, but it received only 62% approval, failing to secure the two-thirds majority of delegates required, and was rejected. B earlier said: "Honestly, the overwhelming sentiment was for rejection. But on the ground, delegates coordinated the numbers. We figured that if it got close to 66.6%, the party wouldn't collapse. There's trauma from Noh Hoe-chan and Shim Sang-jung's defection in 2012 and the Justice Party merger defectors in 2015—we couldn't let the party shrink further." <<> But immediately after the name change failed, Yong and the entire leadership team defected and founded the Basic Income Party. Of course, the aforementioned 'Socialist Party faction underground organization' all moved to the Basic Income Party as well. However, the process by which Yong founded the Basic Income Party and was elected twice as a proportional representative through the Democratic Party of Korea's satellite party appears to have sparked internal backlash as well. C, a source well-versed in progressive camp affairs, said: "Kim Gil-o, who was the underground organization's funding source, fiercely opposed this strategy (the Democratic Party satellite party), and in the end, I understand he cut off financial support." <<> C also pointed out that this is precisely why the Basic Income Party clings to Yong's proportional seat. "The Basic Income Party, which gets little revenue from membership dues of rights-bearing members, depends on Yong's parliamentary seat itself as its livelihood. Don't you see that those who have been together since the underground organization take turns holding party staff and legislative aide positions? Her husband holding a major party post is the least of it." <<> If the Basic Income Party maintains its status as a parliamentary party, it receives approximately 270 million won in regular subsidies every quarter until the next general election. <<> ▷For more articles, see Weekly Chosun. (용혜인 성평등가족부 장관 후보자는 1990년생의 젊은 나이로 비례대표 재선을 지냈다. 그가 지녔던 최초의 정치적 자산은 세월호 참사로 만들어졌다. 경희대에 재학하던 2014년 ‘가만히 있으라’는 이름의 시위를 기획했다는 것이다. 용 후보자는 이때 집회시위법 위반으로 형사처벌까지 받았고, 이 당시 노회찬·심상정 등이 탈당한 진보신당 잔류파와 사회당이 합당해 만든 노동당의 당원이기도 했다.)

item.title: Blocking the Path to Indictment Cancellation, 'Myung-pick Kim Seung-won' Becomes a Burden on the Ruling Camp (공소취소 길 막고 여권의 짐덩이 된 ‘명픽 김승원’)
item.description:
Blocking the Path to Indictment Cancellation, 'Myung-pick Kim Seung-won' Becomes a Burden on the Ruling Camp (공소취소 길 막고 여권의 짐덩이 된 ‘명픽 김승원’)

Suspicions of lobbying on behalf of a pharmaceutical company against Kim Seung-won, the nominee for Minister of Justice, are spreading uncontrollably. Contrary to Kim's explanation of "conveying a public-interest complaint," evidence of shady lobbying surrounding new drug development is emerging one after another. Following allegations of stock price inflation and hit-and-run tactics by the pharmaceutical company's CEO, controversy has now extended to suspicions of a cover-up of the investigation surrounding the suspension of indictment against Kim. (김승원 법무부 장관 후보자의 제약회사 청탁 의혹이 걷잡을 수 없이 확산되고 있습니다. ‘공익적 민원 전달’이라는 김 후보자의 해명과 달리 신약 개발을 둘러싼 검은 로비 정황이 속속 드러나고 있습니다. 제약회사 대표의 주가 부풀리기와 먹튀 의혹이 제기된 데 이어 김 후보자 기소유예 처분을 둘러싼 수사 무마 논란까지 이어지고 있습니다.)

Perhaps that explains it. Kim suddenly began arguing against the possibility of canceling the indictment in President Lee Jae-myung's case. Just recently, he had insisted that the indictment must be canceled, but he changed his stance overnight. The prevailing interpretation is that, cornered by the lobbying suspicions, he made a strategic shift to avoid being rejected during the confirmation hearing. (그래서일까요. 김 후보자는 갑자기 이재명 대통령 사건에 대한 공소 취소 불가론을 폈습니다. 불과 얼마 전까지만 해도 공소 취소를 반드시 해야 한다고 주장했던 그가 하루아침에 입장을 바꾼 것입니다. 로비 의혹으로 궁지에 몰리자 청문회 낙마를 피하기 위해 전략적 변신을 했다는 해석이 유력합니다.)

Within the ruling camp, remarks are circulating that "Kim, a 'Myung-pick,' contrary to initial expectations, is blocking the path to indictment cancellation and becoming a nuclear bomb in the confirmation hearing standoff." The presidential office, which sought to turn the tide through this cabinet reshuffle, has been hobbled by controversies surrounding Kim and candidate Yong Hye-in for Minister of Gender Equality and Family. (여권에선 “‘명픽’인 김 후보자가 당초 기대와는 반대로 공소 취소의 길을 막고 청문 정국의 핵폭탄이 되고 있다”는 말이 나옵니다. 이번 개각을 통해 국면을 전환하려던 청와대는 김 후보자와 용혜인 성평등가족부 장관 후보자 논란으로 발목이 잡혔습니다.)

President Lee's plan to resolve his legal risks has also inevitably hit snags. This is because Kim, fearing he might be the first to fall under the opposition's offensive, has declared, "I will not cancel the indictment." This is likely to deal a significant blow to the administration's morality. The president's approval rating, already down to around 40 percent, could plummet into the 30s. Rather than serving as the president's guardian, he is becoming a burden that trips up the presidential office and the ruling camp. (이 대통령의 사법 리스크 해소 구상도 차질이 불가피해졌습니다. 김 후보자가 야당의 공세로 자신이 먼저 낙마할까 봐 “공소 취소는 안 한다”고 선언해 버렸기 때문입니다. 정권 도덕성에도 적지 않은 타격을 안길 듯합니다. 안 그래도 40% 전후로 떨어진 대통령 지지율은 30%대로 곤두박질칠 수 있습니다. 이 대통령의 호위무사는커녕 청와대와 여권의 발목을 잡는 짐덩이가 되는 분위기입니다.)

The strategy of lying low behind candidate Yong Hye-in has already become untenable. As the opposition's attacks pour in, Kim himself has become the target of arrows. Some observations suggest he may be even harder to save than Yong. 'Myung-pick Kim Seung-won,' once touted as the 'optimal card' to resolve President Lee's legal risks, has now become the biggest risk factor fueling a crisis for the party and the presidential office. (용혜인 후보자 뒤에 숨어서 버티는 전략도 이미 힘들어졌습니다. 야당의 공세가 쏟아지면서 김 후보자 본인이 화살받이 신세가 돼버렸습니다. 용 후보자보다 구명하기가 더 힘들 수 있다는 관측도 나옵니다. 이 대통령 사법 리스크를 해소할 ‘최적의 카드’로 꼽혔던 ‘명픽 김승원’이 당청 위기에 불을 지르는 최대 리스크 요인이 돼버린 형국입니다.)

Kim was considered the right person to resolve the indictment cancellation issue. He was seen as the most trustworthy figure to address President Lee Jae-myung's legal risk problems. However, on the 3rd, Kim said, "I have no intention of canceling the indictment." He stated, "The Minister of Justice does not have direct authority to cancel an indictment," adding, "I also have no intention of exercising command authority (over prosecutors) to cancel it." This is a 180-degree reversal from his previous advocacy of indictment cancellation. (김 후보자는 공소 취소 문제 해결의 적임자로 꼽혔습니다. 이재명 대통령의 사법 리스크 문제를 해결하는 데 가장 신뢰할 수 있는 인물이라는 것입니다. 그런데 김 후보자는 3일 “공소 취소는 할 생각이 없다”고 했습니다. “법무부 장관에게는 직접적인 공소 취소 권한이 없다”며 “(검찰에 공소 취소) 지휘권을 행사할 생각도 없다”고 했습니다. 그동안의 공소 취소 주장과는 180도 달라진 겁니다.)

Not long ago, Kim argued that President Lee's case had been illegally manipulated by prosecutors and that the indictment should be canceled immediately. He served as the head of the Democratic Party's group for indictment cancellation and also proposed a special counsel act for the manipulated indictment. This is likely why he was nominated as Minister of Justice. From the perspective of ordinary citizens, it is baffling how a public official's convictions can change so drastically overnight. (김 후보자는 얼마 전만 해도 이 대통령 사건은 검찰에 의해 불법적으로 조작됐다며 당장 공소를 취소해야 한다고 주장했습니다. 그는 민주당 공소 취소 모임 대표를 맡았고 조작 기소 특검법도 발의했습니다. 법무장관에 지명된 것도 이 때문일 것입니다. 일반 국민들 입장에선 공직자의 소신이 하루아침에 이처럼 달라질 수 있는지 어리둥절할 수밖에 없습니다.)

Kim said, "The stance differs between when one is a lawmaker and when one is a ministerial nominee." However, even if Kim becomes minister, he will concurrently retain his seat as a lawmaker. So, he could say in the morning, as minister, that he cannot cancel the indictment, and then in the evening, as a lawmaker, push for its cancellation. The opposition criticizes this, asking whether two personas can coexist in one body. (김 후보자는 “국회의원일 때와 장관 후보자일 때는 입장이 다르다”고 했습니다. 하지만 김 후보자는 장관이 돼도 국회의원을 겸직합니다. 그러니 아침엔 장관으로서 공소 취소를 못 한다고 했다가 저녁엔 의원으로서 공소 취소에 나설 수도 있습니다. 한 몸에 두 인격이 공존하는 거냐고 야당은 비판합니다.)

Why did Kim suddenly change his position? It is highly likely a strategy of flip-flopping to pass the confirmation hearing. Kim is currently facing criticism as an 'avatar minister under orders to cancel the indictment' and a 'corrupt official who lined the pockets of business operators and brokers through shady lobbying.' Heated debates are expected at the hearing. Hence, the interpretation is that he temporarily retreated to shed the stigma of being a minister for indictment cancellation and get through the hearing. (김 후보자는 왜 갑자기 입장을 바꿨을까요. 인사 청문회 통과를 위한 말 바꾸기 전략일 가능성이 큽니다. 김 후보자는 지금 ‘공소취소 특명을 받은 아바타 장관’ ‘검은 로비로 업자와 브로커 배만 불려준 비위 공직자’라는 비판을 받고 있습니다. 청문회에서도 격론이 예상됩니다. 그래서 일단 공소 취소용 장관이라는 오명을 벗고 청문회를 넘기 위해 일시적으로 후퇴했다는 해석이 나옵니다.)

Another possibility is that Kim may use other methods instead of acting directly. One option is to grant the power of indictment cancellation to the special counsel for the manipulated indictment, which the Democratic Party is pushing, rather than directing prosecutors to cancel it. However, there is strong backlash within the ruling party against this. Critics point out that it is legally inappropriate and politically burdensome for a special counsel to cancel an indictment that should be done by the prosecutors who investigated. (또 하나는 김 후보가 직접 나서는 대신 다른 방법을 쓸 수 있다는 관측입니다. 먼저 검찰에 지시해 공소 취소를 하는 대신 민주당이 추진하는 조작기소 특검에 공소취소권을 주는 방안이 있습니다. 하지만 이에 대해선 여당 내 반발 목소리가 큽니다. 수사한 검찰이 해야 하는 공소 취소를 특검이 하는 건 법적으로 맞지 않고 정치적 부담감도 크다는 지적도 나옵니다.)

Some speculate that a request could be made to the court to dismiss the indictment. However, it is unlikely the court will cancel an indictment that even the prosecution did not. Both options are deemed impractical. (일각에선 법원에 공소 기각을 요청할 수 있다는 관측도 나옵니다. 하지만 검찰도 하지 못한 공소 취소를 법원이 해줄 가능성은 높지 않습니다. 두 가지 다 현실성이 떨어진다는 지적입니다.)

If Kim is appointed minister, will he truly keep his word that he "has no intention of canceling the indictment"? It is true that the minister does not have direct authority to cancel an indictment, but he could push for it by directing the prosecution chief's investigation. The pro-Myung faction expects exactly that. (김 후보자가 만일 장관에 임명된다면 “공소 취소를 할 생각이 없다”고 한 자신의 말을 과연 지킬까요. 장관에게 공소 취소권이 없는 건 맞지만 검찰총장에 대한 수사 지휘를 통해 공소 취소를 밀어붙일 수 있습니다. 친명 진영도 그렇게 기대합니다.)

There's a saying that people differ when entering and leaving the restroom. Once Kim actually becomes minister, he may change his tune again. He could spin a narrative that he had no intention of directing the cancellation, but that pressure from within the prosecution for cancellation grew, leaving him no choice. Even if Kim tries to keep his word, it won't be easy to withstand pressure from the presidential office and the pro-Myung faction to cancel the indictment. (화장실 들어갈 때와 나올 때 다르다는 말이 있죠. 김 후보자가 막상 장관이 되면 다시 말이 달라질 수 있습니다. 자신은 공소 취소를 지휘할 생각이 없었는데, 검찰에서 공소 취소 의견이 커서 어쩔 수 없이 공소 취소를 한다는 식의 논리를 펼 수도 있습니다. 설사 김 후보자가 자기 말을 지키려 해도 청와대와 친명의 공소취소 압박을 버티기가 쉽지 않을 겁니다.)

The problem is that the prosecution chief or prosecutors can refuse. In that case, pushing through the cancellation becomes difficult. While pressure could be applied through a Prosecution Future Committee investigation to withdraw the indictment, there is no evidence that the committee or the truth-finding team has found manipulation or illegal evidence in President Lee's case. (문제는 총장이나 검사가 이를 거부할 수 있다는 겁니다. 이러면 공소취소를 무작정 밀어붙이기가 힘듭니다. 검찰미래위 조사를 통해 공소 취하를 압박할 수는 있지만, 검찰미래위와 진상조사단이 이 대통령 사건에 대한 조작과 불법 증거를 찾았다는 정황은 없습니다.)

Right now, however, Kim seems to have no room to deliberate on the indictment cancellation issue. That is a problem for later. His own lobbying suspicions are the fire at his feet. The more it is stirred, the larger the flames of the lobbying scandal grow. First, photos emerged of Kim, a female broker surnamed Yang, and the warrant judge sharing a drink together. It is said that this same judge rejected the arrest warrant for Kang, the CEO of the pharmaceutical company Genencell, which allegedly received the lobbying. (그런데 지금 김 후보자는 공소취소 문제를 고민할 여유가 없어 보입니다. 이 대통령 사건 공소취소는 나중 문제고요. 본인 로비 의혹이 발등의 불입니다. 파면 팔수록 로비 의혹의 불길은 계속 커지는데요. 먼저 김 후보자와 여성 브로커 양모씨, 영장 판사가 술자리를 함께 하고 동석한 사진이 나왔습니다. 로비를 한 제약회사 제넨셀의 강모 대표 구속영장을 기각한 것도 이 판사라고 합니다.)

Text messages have also surfaced in which Yang called Kim "oppa" and requested that the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety approve clinical trials in line with the company's listing and the attraction of 30 billion won in investment. In this process, Kim allegedly said something to the effect that "once the ministry approves, Genencell could earn hundreds of billions of won." (양씨가 김 후보자를 오빠라고 부르면서 제약회사 상장과 300억원 유치에 맞춰 식약처에 임상시험 승인을 해달라고 청탁하는 문자메시지도 나왔습니다. 이 과정에서 김 후보자는 ‘식약처 승인이 나면 제넨셀은 수천억 원을 벌 수 있다’는 취지로 말했습니다.)

Kim asked the then-commissioner of the Food and Drug Safety Ministry via phone and text to expedite approval of the clinical trials. The commissioner instructed staff to take good care of it. Genencell received approval from the ministry in just 33 days, compared to an average of 142 days for other companies developing COVID-19 treatments. (김 후보자는 당시 식약처장에게 전화와 문자로 빨리 임상 시험 승인을 내달라고 부탁했습니다. 식약처장은 실무 직원들에게 잘 챙기라고 지시했습니다. 제넨셀은 다른 코로나 치료제 개발 회사들이 평균 142일 걸리던 식약처 승인을 단 33일 만에 받아냈습니다.)

Just before the ministry approved the clinical trials, Kang sold Genencell shares to another pharmaceutical company at a high price, pocketing 6.3 billion won. However, the clinical trial data submitted by Genencell was fraudulent, and as a result, the stock fluctuated sharply before its book value dropped to zero. Kim's lobbying not only served to enrich the business operator and broker but also caused significant losses to small investors amid the stock's wild swings. (식약처의 임상 시험 승인이 나기 직전 강씨는 제넨셀 주식을 다른 제약회사에 높은 가격에 매각해 63억원을 챙겼습니다. 하지만 제넨셀이 낸 임상 시험 자료는 허위였고 이 때문에 주가는 급등락하다 장부 가치가 0원이 됐습니다. 김 후보자의 로비가 업자와 브로커 배를 불리는 데 이용됐을 뿐 아니라 주가 급등락으로 소액 투자자들이 큰 피해를 봤습니다.)

Despite this, Kim insists his request was a "public-interest complaint." After the request to the ministry, Kim was set to receive 5 million won in political donations from Kang. Although the donation limit was reached and the money was never actually deposited, he did agree to accept payment for the favor. Nevertheless, Kim avoided punishment through a suspension of indictment. This was because, contrary to the prosecution team's opinion to indict, the Supreme Prosecutors' Office recommended the suspension. (그런데도 김 후보자는 자신의 청탁을 ‘공익 민원’이라고 주장했습니다. 식약처 청탁 후 김 후보자는 강씨로부터 후원금 500만원을 받기로 했습니다. 후원금 한도가 꽉 차서 실제 입금은 안 됐지만 청탁 대가를 받기로 한 것은 맞습니다. 하지만 김 후보자는 기소유예로 처벌을 면했습니다. 당시 수사팀의 기소 의견과 달리 대검이 기소유예 의견을 냈기 때문입니다.)

Not only the opposition but also figures within the ruling camp say it appears difficult for Kim to clear the verification hurdle. This is because the case bears the hallmarks of interest-based lobbying involving large sums of investment, not simple requests, and resembles investment fraud or stock manipulation cases where fraudulent clinical trials caused stock surges and crashes, harming small investors. (야당은 물론이고 여권에서도 김 후보자가 검증의 벽을 넘는 게 쉽지 않아 보인다는 얘기가 나옵니다. 단순 청탁이 아니라 거액의 투자금이 걸린 이권 로비 성격이 짙다는 점, 허위 임상 시험으로 주가가 급등락하고 소액 투자자들이 손해를 본 투자 사기나 주가 조작 사건과 유사하다는 점 때문입니다.)

Initially, the ruling camp's sentiment was to push through Kim's confirmation hearing quickly, even if it meant abandoning candidate Yong Hye-in. Now, however, they are bewildered as the lobbying suspicions grow exponentially. Under normal circumstances, Kim would not have raised the argument against indictment cancellation. The pro-Myung faction would not have stood by either. But now they are quiet. That shows how urgent the situation is. (당초 여권은 용혜인 후보자는 버리더라도 김 후보자 청문회는 속전속결로 끝낸다는 기류였습니다. 그런데 로비 의혹이 일파만파로 커지자 당혹해하고 있습니다. 평상시라면 김 후보자가 공소취소 불가론을 꺼내지도 않았을 겁니다. 친명 진영도 이를 가만히 두고 보지 않았겠죠. 그런데 지금은 조용합니다. 그만큼 다급하다는 얘기입니다.)

The opposition is waging an all-out war to bring down Kim Seung-won. In mid-September, trials for Genencell CEO Kang and broker Yang are scheduled. There is a possibility that Kim will be further cornered. Even if the presidential office unilaterally appoints Kim, he could become a powerless minister, unable to direct prosecutors, let alone pursue indictment cancellation. In the end, rather than serving as the president's guardian, he is being assessed as a burden that damages the administration's morality and fans the flames of an approval-rating crisis. (야당은 ‘김승원 낙마’를 위해 총력전을 펴고 있습니다. 9월 중순엔 제넨셀 강 대표와 브로커 양씨 재판이 예정돼 있습니다. 김 후보자가 더 궁지에 몰릴 가능성이 있습니다. 설령 청와대가 일방적으로 김 후보자를 임명하더라도 공소취소 추진은커녕 검찰 지휘도 하기 힘든 식물 장관이 될 수 있습니다. 결국 이 대통령 호위무사는커녕 정권 도덕성에 타격을 입히고 지지율 위기에 불을 지르는 짐덩이가 되고 있다는 평가입니다.)

item.title: Kang Shin-chul and Brunson of 'Shoulder-Arm-in-Arm' Fame, Now Minister and Commander (‘어깨동무’ 강신철·브런슨, 이젠 장관·사령관으로)
item.description:
Kang Shin-chul and Brunson of 'Shoulder-Arm-in-Arm' Fame, Now Minister and Commander (‘어깨동무’ 강신철·브런슨, 이젠 장관·사령관으로)

Throughout my long career as a newspaper reporter, I have paid close attention to the power and influence a single well-captured photograph can hold. In an era where round-the-clock video seems to overwhelm photography, photos that capture fleeting moments in the flow of time are often more striking than video. They vividly highlight their subjects within history and allow complex situations to be understood at a glance. (오랫동안 신문 기자로 살아오면서 잘 찍힌 사진 한 장이 갖는 힘과 그 영향력에 주목해왔습니다. 24시간 쏟아지는 영상이 사진을 압도하는 시대 같지만, 무심히 흐르는 시간을 포착한 사진은 영상보다 강렬할 때가 적지 않습니다. 역사 속에서 피사체(被寫體)를 선명하게 부각시키며 복잡한 상황을 한 눈에 이해하게 합니다.)

In that regard, the main photo of this article is worth a closer look at a time when the South Korea-U.S. alliance faces multiple challenges. In the photo, taken in March of last year, Kang Shin-chul, the defense minister nominee who served as deputy commander of the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command (CFC), and General Xavier Brunson, commander of U.S. Forces Korea (USFK), are seen laughing heartily with their arms around each other's shoulders. It is a photo that symbolically captures the close relationship between the two men. (그런 점에서 이 기사의 메인 사진은 한미 동맹이 여러 도전에 직면한 현 시점에서 눈여겨볼 만합니다. 지난해 3월 찍힌 사진 속에서 한미연합사 부사령관이었던 강신철 국방부 장관 후보자와 제이비어 브런슨 주한미군사령관이 어깨동무를 하고 활짝 웃고 있습니다. 두 사람의 가까운 관계를 상징적으로 보여주는 사진입니다.)

Commander Brunson has clashed with incumbent Defense Minister An Kyu-baek, who would be replaced if Kang passes his confirmation hearing, over major issues such as the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) and South Korea-U.S. combined exercises, producing considerable discord. In such circumstances, Kang, who formed the CFC leadership with Brunson until just a year ago, has been nominated as the new defense minister. The two men, who once shared meals under the same roof at the CFC, will now meet again in a new dynamic as South Korea's defense minister and the commander of USFK. This is a scene rarely found even in the more than 70-year history of the South Korea-U.S. alliance. (브런슨 사령관은 강 후보자가 인사 청문회를 통과하면 교체될 안규백 국방장관과 전시작전통제권 전환, 한미연합훈련 등 주요 현안을 놓고 이견을 드러내며 적지 않은 불협화음을 빚어왔습니다. 그런 상황에서 불과 1년 전까지 한미연합사에서 자신과 함께 지휘부를 구성했던 강 후보자가 새 국방부 장관으로 지명됐습니다. 한미연합사에서 한솥밥을 먹던 두 사람이 이제 대한민국 국방부 장관과 주한미군사령관이라는 새로운 관계로 다시 만나게 됐습니다. 70년이 넘는 한미동맹사에서도 좀처럼 찾아보기 어려운 장면입니다.)

Commissioned together in 1990, four decades later as the two commanders of the Combined Forces Command (1990년 나란히 임관, 34년 뒤 연합사의 두 대장으로)

Both men were born in the late 1960s and were commissioned as infantry second lieutenants in 1990. Kang Shin-chul began his military career through the Korea Military Academy, while Brunson did so through the ROTC at Hampton University in the United States. More than 30 years later, both had risen to the rank of four-star general in their respective armies. (두 사람은 1960년대 후반 태어나 1990년 나란히 보병 소위로 임관했습니다. 강신철은 한국 육군사관학교, 브런슨은 미국 햄프턴대 ROTC를 거쳐 군 생활을 시작한 후, 30여 년 뒤 각각 육군 대장에 올랐습니다.)

The two generals of the same generation met at the CFC leadership on December 20, 2024. On that day, Brunson succeeded General Paul LaCamera as commander of USFK at Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province. He also assumed the roles of commander of United Nations Command and CFC, as well as Senior U.S. Military Officer Assigned to Korea (SUSMOAK). It is often said that the USFK commander wears four hats, and he consults with the South Korean defense minister on USFK-related matters under the delegation of the U.S. Secretary of Defense and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. (두 동년배 장군이 한미연합사 지휘부에서 만난 것은 2024년 12월 20일이었습니다. 브런슨은 이날 경기도 평택 캠프 험프리스에서 폴 러캐머라의 뒤를 이어 주한미군사령관에 취임했습니다. 유엔군사령관과 한미연합사령관도 동시에 맡았으며 주한미군선임장교(SUSMOAK·Senior U.S. Military Officer Assigned to Korea)를 겸합니다. 흔히 주한미군사령관은 4개의 모자를 쓴다고 하는데, 미 국방 장관, 합참의장의 위임을 받아 주한미군과 관련된 실무를 한국 국방장관과 협의합니다.)

Kang Shin-chul had already been serving as deputy commander of the CFC since October 2023. With Brunson's arrival, a new CFC leadership was launched, with U.S. General Brunson as commander and South Korean General Kang as deputy commander. From the start of his tenure, Brunson emphasized "realistic readiness." He stressed the importance of realistic combined exercises, arguing that deterrence cannot be exercised through words alone. (강신철은 이미 2023년 10월부터 한미연합사 부사령관으로 근무하고 있었습니다. 브런슨이 부임하면서 미군 대장 브런슨이 사령관, 한국군 대장 강신철이 부사령관인 새로운 한미연합사 지휘부가 출범했습니다. 브런슨은 취임 때부터 ‘실전적 대비태세’를 강조했습니다. 말만으로는 억제력을 행사할 수 없다는 취지로 말하며 실전적인 연합훈련의 중요성을 역설했습니다.)

The timing of Brunson's inauguration was far from ordinary. South Korea was in the throes of severe political turmoil immediately following then-President Yoon Suk-yeol's December 3 martial law declaration. Concerns about the combined defense posture were raised as some senior military officials became embroiled in the martial law controversy. Kang was found to have no involvement in the martial law-related investigations. In such circumstances, the newly arrived Brunson and Kang began working in tandem as the top leadership of the CFC. (브런슨의 취임 시기는 예사롭지 않았습니다. 한국은 윤석열 당시 대통령의 12·3 비상계엄 사태 직후 극심한 정치적 혼란을 겪고 있었습니다. 군 수뇌부 일부가 계엄 문제에 휘말리면서 한미 연합방위태세에 대한 우려도 제기됐습니다. 강신철은 계엄 관련 조사에서 연루 사실이 없는 것으로 파악됐습니다. 이런 상황에서 새로 부임한 브런슨과 강신철은 한미연합사의 최고 지휘부로 호흡을 맞추기 시작했습니다.)

A notable public event involving Kang and Brunson together took place at Panmunjom on February 21, 2025. Then-Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Kim Myung-soo, Commander Brunson, and Deputy Commander Kang visited the Joint Security Area (JSA) to inspect the readiness posture along the Military Demarcation Line. (강신철과 브런슨 이 함께 한 대표적인 공개 행사는 2025년 2월 21일 판문점에서 있었습니다. 김명수 당시 합참의장과 브런슨 사령관, 강신철 부사령관은 공동경비구역(JSA)을 찾아 군사분계선 일대의 대비태세를 점검했습니다.)

An impressive photo was taken at the OUllET observation post in Panmunjom. It shows Chairman Kim pointing north with his hand, while Brunson and Kang, standing right beside him, gaze in the same direction. It was the first front-line inspection conducted jointly by the top South Korea-U.S. military brass since Brunson's inauguration. The two continued to visit the field together afterward. On March 6, they jointly observed a South Korea-U.S. combined live-fire exercise at the Seungjin Training Area in Pocheon. (판문점 오울렛 초소에서는 인상적인 사진 한 장이 촬영됐습니다. 김 의장이 북쪽을 손으로 가리키고, 바로 옆에서 브런슨과 강신철이 같은 곳을 바라보는 모습입니다. 브런슨 취임 이후 한미 군 수뇌부가 함께 실시한 첫 최전방 현장 점검이었습니다. 두 사람은 이후에도 현장을 함께 누볐습니다. 3월 6일에는 포천 승진훈련장에서 한미 연합 실사격 훈련을 함께 지켜봤습니다.)

The two men grew closer during the 'Freedom Shield' exercise (‘자유의 방패’ 훈련 함께 하며 가까워진 두 사람)

The most closely coordinated effort between the two was during the South Korea-U.S. combined exercise "Freedom Shield 25," held from March 10 to 20, 2025. It was a large-scale multi-domain combined exercise encompassing land, sea, air, cyber, and space domains. (두 사람이 가장 밀접하게 손발을 맞춘 것은 2025년 3월 10일부터 20일까지 실시된 한미연합연습 ‘자유의 방패(Freedom Shield) 25’였습니다. 육·해·공은 물론 사이버와 우주 영역까지 아우른 대규모 다영역 연합연습이었습니다.)

During the exercise, when Acting President Choi Sang-mok visited CP TANGO, the CFC's wartime command post, they were also together. Acting President Choi was guided by Brunson through the theater operations headquarters, with Kang also present. South Korean and U.S. troops at the site shouted, "Let's go together! We go together!" (훈련 기간 중 최상목 대통령 권한대행이 한미연합사의 전시지휘소인 캠프 탱고(CP TANGO)를 방문했을 때도 함께했습니다. 최 권한대행은 브런슨의 안내를 받아 전구작전본부를 둘러봤고 강신철도 자리를 함께했습니다. 현장의 한미 장병들은 “같이 갑시다! We go together!”를 외쳤습니다.)

As the exercise concluded, Brunson issued a message stating that over the past two weeks, he and Deputy Commander Kang had toured the Freedom Shield exercise sites together and reaffirmed the strength of the South Korea-U.S. alliance and combined defense posture. He also said that from front-line units to strategic discussions, the two allies were ready to fight together at any time. (훈련을 마치면서 브런슨은 지난 2주 동안 강 부사령관과 자유의 방패 연습 현장을 함께 둘러보며 한미동맹과 연합방위태세가 굳건하다는 것을 다시 확인했다는 취지의 메시지를 냈습니다. 최전방 부대부터 전략 토의에 이르기까지 한미가 언제든 함께 싸울 준비가 돼 있다고도 했습니다.)

What drew attention at that time was the "arm-in-arm" photo Brunson released. On March 17, he posted on his social media a photo of himself and Kang standing alone together, arms around each other's shoulders, at Seoul Air Base in Seongnam. The two were seen smiling broadly while standing as close as possible. (이 때 눈길을 끈 것이 브런슨이 공개한 ‘어깨동무’ 사진이었습니다. 그는 3월 17일 성남 서울공항에서 강신철과 어깨 동무를 하고 단둘이 찍은 사진을 자신의 SNS에 올렸습니다. 두 사람이 최대한 밀착해서 활짝 웃는 모습이었습니다.)

It drew interest because LaCamera, the previous USFK commander, had rarely, if ever, released such photos with the CFC deputy commander. According to a report by Yang Ji-ho of the Chosun Ilbo, a military official said, "Over the past two weeks, Commander Brunson built rapport with Deputy Commander Kang while conducting field guidance together," adding, "It appears to reflect the new commander's determination to actively promote the South Korea-U.S. alliance and communicate with the South Korean public." (직전 주한미군사령관이었던 폴 러캐머라가 연합사 부사령관과 이런 사진을 공개한 전례가 거의 없었다는 점에서 관심을 끌었습니다. 조선일보 양지호 기자의 보도에 따르면 군 관계자는 “지난 2주 동안 브런슨 사령관이 강 부사령관과 현장지도를 다니며 공감대를 쌓았다”며 “한미동맹을 적극적으로 알리고 대한민국 국민과 소통하려는 신임 사령관의 의지가 반영된 것으로 보인다”고 했습니다.)

The joint activities of the two continued. When Acting President Han Duck-soo visited Camp Humphreys on April 23 of last year, Brunson and Kang together briefed on the South Korea-U.S. alliance and combined defense posture. Looking back, the two men led the top command of the CFC together during a period of extreme political turmoil in South Korea. Whenever acting presidents visited the CFC and USFK, the two sent messages that the South Korea-U.S. combined defense posture remained unshaken. Through this process, they likely gained deep insight into each other's military judgment and command styles. (두 사람의 공동 행보는 계속됐습니다. 지난해 4월 23일 한덕수 대통령 권한대행이 캠프 험프리스를 방문했을 때도 브런슨과 강신철은 함께 한미동맹과 연합방위태세를 설명했습니다.돌이켜보면 두 사람은 한국 정치가 극심한 혼란을 겪던 시기에 한미연합사의 최고 지휘부를 함께 맡았습니다. 대통령 권한대행이 잇따라 연합사와 주한미군을 찾을 때마다 두 사람은 한미연합방위태세에 흔들림이 없다는 메시지를 발신했습니다. 이 과정에서 서로의 군사적 판단과 지휘 스타일을 깊숙이 파악했을 것으로 보입니다.)

On August 20 of last year, a photo was taken at CP TANGO that, in hindsight, carries a peculiar significance. During the Ulchi Freedom Shield (UFS) exercise, Defense Minister An Kyu-baek visited the wartime command post. The released photo shows Minister An, Commander Brunson, and Deputy Commander Kang walking and conversing together. About a year later, no one would have predicted that Deputy Commander Kang would be nominated as Minister An's successor. The relationship among the three men captured in a single photo back then has now changed dramatically. (지난해 8월 20일 캠프 탱고에서는 지금 돌이켜보면 묘한 사진이 찍혔습니다. ‘을지 자유의 방패(UFS)’ 연습 기간에 안규백 국방장관이 전시지휘소를 방문했습니다. 공개된 사진에는 안 장관과 브런슨 사령관, 강신철 부사령관이 함께 걸으며 대화하는 모습이 담겼습니다. 그로부터 약 1년 뒤 강 부사령관이 안 장관의 후임으로 지명될 것이라고 예상한 사람은 없었을 겁니다. 당시 한 장의 사진에 함께 담겼던 세 사람의 관계가 이제 크게 달라지게 됐습니다.)

When Kang Shin-chul retired from the military in September 2025 after completing his term as CFC deputy commander, Brunson praised him, saying, "General Kang's leadership, rooted in the conviction that the South Korea-U.S. alliance is forged in the blood of comrades-in-arms, has further strengthened our readiness through realistic and relentless training." He added, "It was an honor to serve alongside General Kang Shin-chul." These words, too strong to be dismissed as mere ceremonial farewell remarks, suggest the considerable trust built between them. (브런슨은 2025년 9월 강신철이 한미연합사 부사령관을 마치고 전역할 때 “한미동맹이 전우들의 피로 맺어졌다는 신념에 뿌리를 둔 강 장군의 리더십은 현실적이고 끊임없는 훈련을 통해 우리의 대비태세를 더욱 강화했다”고 평가했습니다. 이어 “강신철 장군과 함께 복무할 수 있어서 영광이었다”고 했습니다. 의례적인 환송사로만 보기에는 강한 표현으로 상당한 신뢰를 쌓았음을 짐작하게 합니다.)

This time, they sit across from each other over 'wartime OPCON' (이번에는 ‘전작권’을 놓고 마주 앉는다)

However, the issues the two must now address as minister and commander are entirely different in nature from those of the past. At the center lies the transfer of wartime operational control. Brunson has consistently supported the OPCON transfer in principle while emphasizing the "condition fulfillment" requirement. When he met with South Korean reporters at Camp Humphreys in August 2025, he warned that taking a "shortcut" without meeting the necessary conditions could endanger the military readiness posture on the Korean Peninsula. In April of this year, he stressed to the U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee that "political convenience must not precede conditions." The following day, he told the House Armed Services Committee that the two allies are pursuing a roadmap aimed at meeting the conditions for OPCON transfer by the first quarter of 2029 at the latest. (하지만 두 사람이 장관과 사령관으로 다시 만나 다뤄야 할 현안은 과거와 성격이 전혀 다릅니다. 그 중심에 전시작전통제권 전환 문제가 있습니다. 브런슨은 전작권 전환 자체에는 찬성하면서도 ‘조건 충족’이라는 원칙을 일관되게 강조해왔습니다. 2025년 8월 캠프 험프리스에서 한국 기자들을 만났을 때는 필요한 조건을 충족하지 않은 채 ‘지름길’을 택하면 한반도의 군사대비 태세를 위험하게 만들 수 있다고 경고했습니다. 올해 4월 미 상원 군사위원회에서는 “정치적 편의가 조건보다 앞서서는 안 된다”고 강조했습니다. 다음 날 하원 군사위원회에서는 한미가 전작권 전환에 필요한 조건을 늦어도 2029년 1분기까지 충족하는 것을 목표로 한 로드맵을 추진하고 있다고 밝혔습니다.)

In such circumstances, Kang Shin-chul, who had been serving as ambassador to Saudi Arabia after his retirement, returned to South Korea after only six months and was nominated as Minister An's successor. One of the questions Kang received on the 3rd, when he first reported for work to prepare for his confirmation hearing, concerned the OPCON transfer. He said, "The OPCON transfer will be pursued in a direction that strengthens the South Korea-U.S. alliance," adding, "Without the South Korea-U.S. alliance, the concept of OPCON transfer would not even exist." (이런 상황에서 전역 후 주사우디아라비아 대사로 부임했던 강신철이 불과 6개월 만에 귀국해 안규백 장관의 후임으로 지명됐습니다. 강 후보자가 지난 3일 인사청문회 준비를 위해 처음 출근하면서 받은 질문 중 하나는 전작권 전환이었습니다. 그는 “전작권 전환은 한미동맹이 강화되는 방향으로 추진할 것”이라며 “한미동맹이 없었다면 전작권 전환은 존재하지도 않는 개념”이라고 했습니다.)

Based on their public statements so far, it is difficult to see the two men's positions as being in direct conflict. Brunson emphasizes that "conditions must not be skipped." Kang says, "The transfer should be carried out in a direction that strengthens the South Korea-U.S. alliance." The fact that Kang, having co-led the CFC with Brunson, understands Brunson's mindset as well as the U.S. military's perspective on the OPCON issue better than anyone else could be a significant asset in future South Korea-U.S. consultations. (현재까지 공개된 발언만 보면 두 사람의 입장이 정면으로 충돌한다고 보기는 어렵습니다. 브런슨은 ‘조건을 건너뛰어서는 안 된다’​고 강조합니다. 강신철은 ‘한미동맹을 강화하는 방향으로 전환해야 한다’​고 합니다. 강 후보자가 브런슨과 한미연합사를 함께 이끌면서 그의 사고방식은 물론 미군이 전작권 문제를 바라보는 시각을 누구보다 잘 알고 있다는 점은 향후 한미 협의 때 중요한 자산이 될 수 있습니다.)

The variable is President Lee Jae-myung's pressure for 'early transfer' (변수는 이재명 대통령의 ‘조기 전환’ 압박)

The problem lies in President Lee Jae-myung's pressure for an "early transfer." President Lee, who views the OPCON transfer as a matter of sovereignty restoration, rebuked Defense Minister An Kyu-baek in May with remarks to the effect that "we should ensure there are no problems even if OPCON is transferred tomorrow." The prospect of having to find common ground between the president's resolve and the U.S. position emphasizing "condition fulfillment" is expected to place considerable burden on Kang. (문제는 이재명 대통령의 ‘조기 전환’ 압박입니다. 전작권 전환을 주권 회복 차원에서 바라보는 이 대통령은 지난 5월 “내일 전작권을 전환해도 아무런 문제가 없도록 해야 한다”는 취지의 발언을 하며 안규백 국방장관을 질책했습니다. 대통령의 이러한 의지와 ‘조건 충족’을 강조하는 미국 측의 입장 사이에서 접점을 찾아야 한다는 점은 강 후보자에게 적지 않은 부담이 될 전망입니다.)

Until last year, Kang Shin-chul, as CFC deputy commander, formed a single command with Brunson and moved toward the same goal. But now, as defense minister, he must consult with Brunson on the timing and conditions of the OPCON transfer, the role of USFK, and the future of the South Korea-U.S. combined defense system from the perspective of the South Korean government. When their interests align, they will join hands, but when South Korean and U.S. judgments diverge, their relationship has become one in which each must persuade the other. (지난해까지만 해도 강신철은 연합사 부사령관으로 브런슨과 하나의 지휘부를 이루며 같은 목표를 향해 움직였습니다. 하지만, 이제 국방부 장관이 되면 대한민국 정부의 입장에서 전작권 전환의 시기와 조건, 주한미군의 역할, 한미연합방위체제의 미래를 놓고 브런슨과 협의해야 합니다. 이해가 일치할 때는 손을 맞잡겠지만, 한국과 미국의 판단이 엇갈릴 때는 서로를 설득해야 하는 관계가 됐습니다.)

Will the trust of the past, symbolized by the arm-in-arm photo, become an asset in resolving the sensitive challenges of the South Korea-U.S. alliance? Or will two men who know each other too well find themselves standing more fiercely across from each other over the future of the alliance, including OPCON? The bond between the two generals, captured in a single photograph a year and a half ago, now faces a new test for the South Korea-U.S. alliance. (어깨동무 사진으로 상징되는 과거의 신뢰가 한미동맹의 민감한 난제를 풀어가는 자산이 될 것인가. 아니면 서로를 너무 잘 아는 두 사람이 전작권을 비롯한 동맹의 미래를 놓고 더 치열하게 마주 서게 될 것인가. 1년 반 전 사진 한 장에 담긴 두 장군의 인연이 이제 한미동맹의 새로운 시험대에 오르게 됐습니다.)
